newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIAN LEAGUE PROBES POSSIBLE MATCH-FIXING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIAN LEAGUE PROBES POSSIBLE MATCH-FIXING.

text.p: Russian soccer officials are set to meet on Monday to review allegations of match-fixing in a premier league game last week, a senior league director said on Thursday.
An independent Expert Council will look at material passed on by official observers at the July 23 match at Sochi, when the home side Zhemchuzhina beat long-time rivals Chernomorets Novorossiisk 3-1.
League executive director Vitaly Krechetov did not say what prompted the suspicions of dishonesty.
Zhemchuzhina coach Arsen Naidyonov fiercely denied any fixing and accused the soccer elite in Moscow of conspiring against provincial sides.
The Sochi club, currently lying eighth in the table two points behind fourth-placed Chernomorets, would not be sending a representative to Monday's hearing, he told Reuters.
"Dark forces in the capital are scheming against strong teams from the provinces," Naidyonov said.
Rumours of match-fixing have long been rife in Soviet and now Russian soccer.
Earlier this year the league set up a special commission to deal with match-fixing allegations by reviewing video and other evidence. It has the power to instigate criminal proceedings.
League president Nikolai Tolstykh, who is also chairman of Dynamo Moscow, promised a crackdown on corruption this season, urging clubs not to let financial pressure undermine fair play.

Second-division Iriston Vladikavkaz, from the turbulent North Caucasus region, were thrown out of the league last year for trying to rig a match. It was one of the first cases of its kind. They were later reinstated in a lower division.

Allegations of links between soccer and Russia's organised crime gangs were fuelled in June when the woman who ran the business activities of champions Spartak Moscow was gunned down in a mafia-style hit outside the capital.
